subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue these as core/gateway APIs now, and if so which track should become the first canonical design: tool batching, context block lifecycle, or runner-owned plan enforcement?
rationale: The request adds new model-visible tools, config/default behavior, persistence semantics, and runner policy; automation cannot safely choose those product and compatibility contracts.

options.title: Split Into Maintainer Design Tracks
options.body: Keep the umbrella open, then define separate reviewed contracts for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before any implementation PR.

options.title: Narrow To Context Lifecycle First
options.body: Use the related context-clearing work as the first canonical design and defer batching and plan enforcement until the session lifecycle contract is settled.

options.title: Decline Core Enforcement For Now
options.body: Keep current update_plan, compaction, context-engine, and plugin surfaces as the supported path while declining new strict core orchestration APIs.

recommendation.title: Split Into Maintainer Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open, then define separate reviewed contracts for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history across update_plan, strict-agentic behavior, web-search tooling, and the prior keep-open review for this issue.
